title: Fabric Data Warehouse at Ignite: Built for AI-era analytics
author: tinotereshko

content.text:
If you haven’t already, read Arun Ulag’s Ignite blog post to learn how Microsoft is bringing together databases, analytics, and intelligent applications across Azure and Microsoft Fabric.
Our telemetry shows that agentic analytics has arrived. Agents query, investigate, iterate, test, and drill down without waiting for human input. This machine-paced activity pushes analytical engines built for human-paced workloads to their limits. Fabric Data Warehouse was built from scratch in the 2020s to support this new interaction model, combining highly scalable serverless compute, a resilient lakehouse architecture, and integration across Fabric.
At Ignite, we’re building on that foundation for agents and the people who rely on them. The updates focus on performance at agentic scale, better interoperability with AI, and richer capabilities for warehouse development and operations.
Scale performance for agentic investigation
When queries wait, agentic investigations pause. We’re improving Fabric Data Warehouse performance on three fronts:
• Fresh OneLake metadata.
• A faster, more efficient engine.
• Workload controls that help you balance performance and cost.
Keep SQL analytics endpoint metadata fresh
The new metadata sync for the SQL analytics endpoint is now generally available. Tables in OneLake are always visible to the SQL analytics endpoint, and queries return fresh data. This release includes:
• A straightforward upgrade path from existing SQL analytics endpoints.
• Metadata refreshes within seconds and at query time, so queries always see the latest data.
• Large object type(LOB) and time travel support.
• Compatibility with Delta checkpoint V2.
Figure: Animated GIF - demonstrating performance of the new SQL analytics endpoint metadata sync.
A faster, more efficient engine
In recent days we’ve rolled out a rebuilt distributed shuffle to accelerate data movement between query nodes, along with enhanced task scheduling to improve resource use and speed up query tasks. Combined with several earlier innovations, such as distributed bitmap filters and usage-based resource estimation corrections, these changes have improved Fabric Data Warehouse performance by 70% on an industry-standard benchmark[footnoteRef:1] over the past year.
Figure: Fabric Data Warehouse performance improvements over time.
Controls tailored to your workloads
User workloads have varying demands. Some need cached data to stay warm between bursts; others need predictable resource boundaries or acceleration for latency-sensitive analytics. These controls help you make those trade-offs:
• Cache cooldown (coming in January 2027) lets you control how long data stays cached at the SQL pool level. Keep data warm between intermittent activity or shorten retention to reduce idle allocation and cost.
• On-demand billing (Preview) offers consumption-based billing with capacity-level budget controls and workspace-level ceilings. Data Warehouse consumption is separate from other workload categories. When a workspace reaches its ceiling, queries queue and resume as resources become available.
• Custom SQL pools (Generally Avaiable), let you set maximum resource shares and separate workloads by application or statement type. Tune SELECT and non-SELECT allocations to match your read/write needs.
• GPU-based query acceleration (Limited Preview) targets high-concurrency analytical workloads where latency matters, including interactive reporting and AI-driven exploration. Released in August, it delivers roughly twice the performance at one-third lower cost than competing offerings on a 300GB DirectQuery benchmark.
Connect Fabric Data Warehouse to the agents you use
Develop, query, and operate through AI tools
A faster warehouse is even more useful when AI agents can work with it directly. The remote Data Warehouse MCP server gives agents secure high-quality access to your data warehouses. Agent Skills for Microsoft Fabric provide specialized guidance for developing, querying, and operating Fabric items.
Together, MCP and Agent Skills bring agent-driven warehouse development, analytics, and operations into the AI tools developers already use. With warehouse-specific capabilities and expertise, agents can carry out end-to-end tasks: explore schemas, write SQL, troubleshoot queries, and manage warehouse workloads.
Figure: Bring your own AI tool to Fabric Data Warehouse.
Ground answers in shared business context
Fabric IQ integration uses ontologies to connect warehouse data with shared business models, concepts, and relationships. This enables Fabric data agents to provide natural-language answers grounded in governed enterprise data. Publish the agents to Teams, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, or custom endpoints to bring insights into the tools where people work and make decisions.
Build, operate, and modernize your warehouse with confidence
Modern workloads need more than speed and agent access. They also need expressive SQL, clear operational visibility, and dependable tooling for development, governance, and migration.
Monitor workloads and troubleshoot queries
• Workspace monitoring integration, brings warehouses into a shared view and connects workspace-level signals with individual queries.
• Graphical query plan (coming soon) and Live Query Troubleshooting (Limited Preview) show plans before execution and activity during execution, helping you identify expensive operators and data movement.
• SQL pool insights enhancements provide near-real-time vNode usage metrics, making compute usage and pool pressure easier to understand.
• DW monitor enhancements (coming soon) add diagnostic cards that highlight key workload signals and point you to the next troubleshooting step.
• Operations agent skills help investigate capacity spikes, recommend SQL pools, assess table health, and analyze failures.
Write more expressive SQL and simplify development
• T-SQL enhancements reduce repetition and simplify window-function filtering with FROM-first queries, GROUP BY ALL, and QUALIFY.
• Regular expressions and analytical aggregates support pattern matching, replacement, and extraction through REGEXP_LIKE, REGEXP_REPLACE, and REGEXP_SUBSTR. For exact and approximate distribution analysis, use MEDIAN, QUANTILE, APPROX_MEDIAN, and APPROX_QUANTILE.
• User-defined Functions support richer procedural logic with branches, loops, BREAK, and CONTINUE. Eligible functions are inlined, with creation-time checks, actionable errors, control-flow resource estimation, and plan visibility.
• Fabric User Data Functions integration lets T-SQL call published Python functions to work with APIs, files, configuration, and other Fabric data.
• Richer data and table support adds VARCHAR(MAX) and VARBINARY(MAX) to the SQL analytics endpoint, supporting text, JSON, logs, and binary content.
• The SQL web experience introduces table overviews, a no-code table designer, and interactive result visualizations. Redesigned Object Explorer and results grids and improved IntelliSense round out the experience.
Figure: Summary of SQL enhancement announcements.
Develop, deploy, and govern with greater control
• Warehouse Clones (Limited Private Preview) create point-in-time, read/write environments within or across workspaces and capacities, without an initial full copy. Use them to separate development, testing, reporting, and recovery. Refresh a clone to a newer restore point while retaining its item and endpoint. Sign up to join the Limited Private Preview.
Figure: Animated GIF - Demonstration of cross-workspace warehouse cloning in Microsoft Fabric.
• CI/CD 2.0 with DacFx provides schema-aware deployment and item-definition lifecycle automation for Warehouse and SQL analytics endpoint workflows. Use pre- and post-deployment scripts for preparation and validation, and Schema Compare in VS Code to review object differences before deployment.
• Connectivity and security improvements cover client connections, permissions, identity, and auditing:
• A more direct client-to-compute path for Private Link workspaces.
• OneLake group registration and column-permission propagation.
• SQL analytics endpoint user mapping.
• Audit-log predicate filtering.
• Workspace identity for ingestion.
• Workspace server aliases (coming in December) provide customer-defined endpoint names to help manage connections and recovery for workspaces with private link.
Migration tools for warehouse modernization
• Incremental migration in Migration Assistant lets you move selected objects into an existing destination in waves. Resolve conflicts with skip, overwrite, or rename options.
• Teradata support converts uploaded tables, views, functions, macros, and stored procedures. BTEQ conversion brings scripts into stored-procedure workflows.
• The Synapse dedicated SQL pool migration skill provides agent-assisted guidance for moving existing warehouse code to Fabric.
A foundation for agents and warehouse teams
AI is rapidly changing how organizations are performing analytics. Fabric Data Warehouse at Ignite is moving in that direction: supporting machine-paced analytics while improving everyday warehouse work for the people who build and operate it. We can’t wait for you to try out all the new capabilities we’re shipping in Fabric Data Warehouse.
• Join the Fabric DW Community and share your feedback with us.
• Catch the rest of the Fabric announcements in the Fabric November 2026 Feature Summary.
• Join us at our next Fabric and SQL Community Conferences: Atlanta | Sydney (use code MSCUST to save on registration).
